name: xkbcommon

engine.notes: "direct-compile", matching libcrtgfx/third_party/wayland/recipe.json's own established shape exactly (same reasoning: no Meson/Ninja host-tool dependency, tools/build_xkbcommon.py drives every compile/link step itself via tools/crt-cc). The one real difference from Wayland's own build: libxkbcommon's core library has exactly one generated-file requirement (src/xkbcomp/parser.y, a real bison/yacc grammar) that this project cannot regenerate itself without a new, disproportionately large bison-as-host-tool port -- see generated/README.md for the full reasoning and provenance. That single file is pre-generated and committed at libcrtgfx/third_party/xkbcommon/generated/{parser.c,parser.h}; tools/build_xkbcommon.py copies it into place rather than invoking bison.

notes: Added 2026-08-25 as Phase 3 of the "notepad-capability" plan (real keyboard input, following the explicit user directive to do the Linux/Wayland side of input handling before Windows/macOS): wl_keyboard's own wire protocol only ever hands a client a raw evdev keycode plus a compositor-supplied XKB keymap string (see src/arch/linux/window_wayland.c's own wl_seat/wl_keyboard wiring) -- libxkbcommon is the real, de facto standard library (used by GTK, Qt, every wlroots-based compositor, ...) that turns that pair into an actual character/keysym plus real modifier-state tracking. Scope: the core xkb_context/xkb_keymap/xkb_state API only (src/*.c, src/xkbcomp/*.c) -- xkbregistry (a separate UI-layout-picker library, its own recipe.json's own "schema shape matches" convention aside, genuinely unrelated to processing key events) and the Compose/dead-key subsystem (src/compose/*, confirmed by a real grep that no core keymap/state file references it at all) are both deferred; neither is needed to turn a wl_keyboard::key event into real UTF-8 text.

Version 1.9.2 (2025-05-06), the current stable release at recipe-creation time. source.ref/source.expected_commit are the real commit github.com/xkbcommon/libxkbcommon.git's own `xkbcommon-1.9.2` annotated tag dereferences to, captured via `git ls-remote https://github.com/xkbcommon/libxkbcommon.git refs/tags/xkbcommon-1.9.2 refs/tags/xkbcommon-1.9.2^{}` on 2026-08-25 (the `^{}` form is the annotated tag's own dereferenced commit SHA, not the tag object's own SHA -- `dd642359f8d43c09968e34ca7f1eb1121b2dfd70`, not `67ac6792bda0fd9ef0ae17a4c33026d17407b325`) -- matching libcrtgfx/third_party/wayland/recipe.json's own established pinning discipline exactly, including the re-pin instructions.

GitHub's own Releases page for this project ships no dist tarball at all (confirmed via the real GitHub API: `"assets": []` on the xkbcommon-1.9.2 release) -- unlike expat/freetype, there is no richer, pre-generated archive to fetch instead of a plain git checkout; a git clone at the pinned commit really is the most complete source available.

The one real generated-file requirement (src/xkbcomp/parser.y, a bison/yacc grammar producing parser.c/parser.h) is NOT regenerated by this project's own build -- pre-generated once and committed at generated/parser.c and generated/parser.h, see that directory's own README.md for the exact command, bison version, and re-pin discipline. This project's own sandboxed dev environment had no bison installed and no interactive sudo to install one; the user installed it themselves in their own terminal for this one-time generation. Every other build system this project owns (tools/crt-cc itself, the whole crt-port-build.py configure/amalgamation/android_host_tool engine, tools/build_wayland.py) deliberately has zero host-tool dependency beyond the C compiler -- porting bison itself as a new host-tool build (a large, general-purpose parser-generator project, wildly out of proportion to what one grammar file needs) was considered and rejected in favor of this narrower, one-time fix.

keywords.c (src/xkbcomp/keywords.c) is ALSO gperf-generated upstream, but ships pre-committed directly in the real git checkout itself (confirmed: `grep gperf meson.build` finds no generator()/custom_target() invoking gperf at build time at all -- meson.build just lists it as a plain source file) -- no action needed for this one, it just gets compiled as-is like any other .c file.

config.h's own real HAVE_* macros (this project's own tools/build_xkbcommon.py hand-writes it directly, matching tools/build_wayland.py's own generate_config_header() precedent, rather than needing Meson's configure_file()) were set only after checking this project's own libc headers directly, not assumed from a generic Linux config: HAVE_UNISTD_H/HAVE___BUILTIN_EXPECT/HAVE_MMAP always on (real, always-present PAL surface); HAVE_STRNDUP/HAVE_ASPRINTF/HAVE_VASPRINTF/HAVE_OPEN_MEMSTREAM/HAVE_EACCESS all real, confirmed functions in this project's own include/string.h, include/stdio.h, include/unistd.h; HAVE_SECURE_GETENV/HAVE___SECURE_GETENV/HAVE_EUIDACCESS/HAVE_MKOSTEMP left unset (confirmed real GNU-only extensions this project's own Bionic-style libc does not provide) -- each one falls back to a real, portable, already-present alternative in libxkbcommon's own source (secure_getenv -> plain getenv, confirmed by reading src/utils.h's own #if/#define chain directly; HAVE_MKOSTEMP/HAVE_POSIX_FALLOCATE are not referenced by any real core-library source file at all, confirmed via a direct grep -- dead config entries for this build, not a real gap). PATH_MAX set to 4096 (this project's own Linux limits.h value, confirmed elsewhere in this codebase's own porting work).

DFLT_XKB_CONFIG_ROOT is set to the real, standard /usr/share/X11/xkb path (Linux only) -- this is NOT something this port bundles or generates: real XKB keymap text a compositor hands a client over wl_keyboard::keymap can itself contain `include` directives (xkbcomp's own keymap-dump format does not necessarily flatten them away), which xkb_keymap_new_from_buffer() needs to resolve against a real system XKB data tree exactly the way every other real Wayland/X11 client (GTK, Qt, ...) already does -- confirmed the xkb-data package (providing this exact directory) is a real, already-installed, completely standard system dependency on this session's own WSL host, not something unusual to assume present. This is data, not code -- no different in kind from this project's own existing reliance on host CA certificates for mbedTLS/curl.

xkb_state_update_key() is deliberately never called anywhere in this port's own consumer wiring (src/arch/linux/window_wayland.c) -- confirmed by reading its own doc comment directly: "This entry point is intended for *server* applications and should not be used by *client* applications". A real Wayland client instead calls xkb_state_update_mask() with the mods_depressed/mods_latched/mods_locked/group fields wl_keyboard::modifiers already hands it, and reads xkb_state_key_get_utf8()/xkb_state_key_get_syms() against whatever state that produces -- xkb_state_update_key() is for a *compositor* tracking key state itself, a role this project's own client-side backend never plays.

Keycode offset: wl_keyboard::key's own raw keycode is a Linux evdev code (matching this project's own crtgfx_event.key.keycode public-API numbering, see crtgfx/window.h's own design comment); xkbcommon's own keycode space is offset by +8 from evdev (confirmed directly in wayland.xml's own wl_keyboard::keymap event doc: "to determine the xkb keycode, clients must add 8 to the key event keycode", a real, historical X11-compatibility offset xkbcommon inherited). src/arch/linux/window_wayland.c adds this +8 only at the xkbcommon call boundary -- the public crtgfx_event API never sees it.
